## About the study

This project estimates the carbon intensity (CI) that Nebraska producers can expect for their crops and for the co-products fed to beef cattle.

## Objective

Estimate the expected life-cycle CI of corn and soybeans produced in Nebraska, by region and irrigation, and extend those estimates to distillers grains with solubles (DGS) and soybean meal (SBM).

## Methods

- Two life-cycle assessment models: GREET FD-CIC (U.S. Department of Energy) and IFSM (U.S. Department of Agriculture).
- Three Nebraska regions (West, Central, East), each with irrigated and rainfed production.
- Value-based allocation of emissions between co-products (ethanol and DGS; soybean oil and SBM).

## Main results

- **Corn:** expected CI of 0.29 (IFSM) and 0.25 (GREET) lb CO₂e per lb of grain dry matter, close to the U.S. default of 0.297.
- **Soybeans:** expected CI of 0.28 (IFSM) and 0.32 (GREET), compared with a U.S. default of 0.338.
- **Irrigation:** irrigated corn and soybeans have roughly 10% lower CI than rainfed crops.
- **Distillers grains:** drying raises CI. Modified DGS is about 23% higher than wet DGS, and dry DGS is about 50% higher (weighted averages of 0.20–0.23 for wet, 0.25–0.28 for modified, and 0.31–0.33 for dry DGS).
- **Soybean meal:** expected CI of 0.36 (IFSM) and 0.38 (GREET) kg CO₂e per kg of dry matter.
